authority: Direct human feedback. Uncertainty and tentative terms are retained.

annotations.question_context: Which two real datasets or analysis tasks should drive the next round of features?
annotations.user_feedback: We should be pushing in several directions: deep engineering and technical analysis (imagine analysis on data collected from a science or engineering experiment). I may not have great datasets in place. I had a separate worktree that is looking into that right now.
annotations.resolution: Prioritize engineering and scientific end-user work. Dataset availability is uncertain; user reports separate investigation.

annotations.question_context: If we could deliver only three improvements, which would you choose?
annotations.user_feedback: editorial style, edit in place, scatter matrix, and table usability. time is important but cuts across a couple things, so would improve in a second pass
annotations.resolution: Accept four first-pass priorities without forcing a three-feature limit. Time is second-pass.

annotations.question_context: When priorities conflict, should your own investigations, charts you publish, or developers embedding explorEDA win?
annotations.user_feedback: The goal is to produce the most powerful platform for END USERS. Developers use the tool to deliver an experience to end users. We work for the user.
annotations.resolution: End users determine product choices; developers deliver the experience.

annotations.question_context: Where do you want finished editorial charts to go?
annotations.user_feedback: We need the interative workspace to "feel" editorial. So all the current features with a little better types and layout. I also wnat to be able to export to images and possibly slides or a PDF report. Think through how to handle export sutff... but that should really be a new intent with a dedicated scope: please create that too
annotations.resolution: Editorial experience is live. Create dedicated image-export intent; slide and PDF outputs remain possibilities.

annotations.question_context: Which existing charts or design systems best represent the look you want?
annotations.user_feedback: Newspapers: financial times, economist, washington post, NY Times. From there, I am thinking abotu the pretty things put together by consulatnts in end of year or investor relation docs.
annotations.resolution: Record named visual references. No specific page, font, or layout is selected.

annotations.question_context: When a host’s theme changes, should saved charts follow that change or retain their original authored appearance?
annotations.user_feedback: Yes, things should be linked to a global set of colors or theme. They update automatically (unless intentioanlly overridden). Make iti easy to spot overrides too on some screen
annotations.resolution: Automatic global theme links, intentional local overrides, and a findable override view are selected behavior.

annotations.question_context: Which three edits would save you the most time?
annotations.user_feedback: Text and axis. Text supports readability and "creating a quick dashboard". Basically, opening the settings menu is a chore, so any "direct" edit is a huge time savings.
annotations.resolution: Prioritize direct text and axis edits for readability and quick dashboard creation.

annotations.question_context: Should edits change the chart immediately?
annotations.user_feedback: Change immediately. we have robust undo, so there's minimal risk there
annotations.resolution: Apply valid changes immediately and reuse existing undo. Do not impose a preview acceptance stage.

annotations.question_context: What is the matrix’s main job?
annotations.user_feedback: Making sense of a multivaraiate data set where you may not know how things are related at the start. It's a very nice "start here" sort of data viz.
annotations.resolution: Matrix is an exploration starting point for unfamiliar multivariate data.

annotations.question_context: With missing values, should each cell show every usable observation, or should every cell use the same complete records?
annotations.resolution: Explain pairwise versus complete-case populations with an example. Recommend pairwise use provisionally; no user selection inferred.

annotations.question_context: What row count and number of fields would you normally put in a matrix?
annotations.user_feedback: idk, 10k-100k rows. Presuambly we need to go to a canvas renderer at some point (if not already?).
annotations.resolution: Record tentative row target and verify current Canvas renderer. Field count and latency remain unspecified.

annotations.question_context: Comparisons, metrics, and time: which baseline and how should it change with the source?
annotations.user_feedback: I think I hve minimal interest in this comparison thing. Let's de-rate it.
annotations.resolution: Lower named-comparison priority; do not pause or cancel the initiative.

annotations.question_context: Which calculation currently sends you to another tool?
annotations.user_feedback: Not sure yet, havent used tool enough.
annotations.resolution: Demand for additional measures remains unconfirmed. Keep as a seed.

annotations.question_context: After brushing one matrix cell, should the other cells show only matching records or retain all observations and highlight matches?
annotations.user_feedback: Brushing one cell should probably dim the unrelated cells. Basically brushing = setting a filter on 2 dims.
annotations.resolution: Record tentative preference for two-field filtering with dimmed nonmatching context. Interpret observations rather than whole cells provisionally.

annotations.question_context: Which missing selection capability matters first?
annotations.user_feedback: Lasso would be really nice. The filters without a chart would also be really nice.
annotations.resolution: Lasso and chart-free filters have direct expressed interest. Other selection proposals do not inherit the same priority.

annotations.question_context: When reusing an analysis, which choices should carry forward?
annotations.user_feedback: I think all of those? idk
annotations.resolution: Tentatively preserve full analysis state. Do not infer a filter-free template requirement.

annotations.question_context: Which result would you most want to use as another chart’s input?
annotations.user_feedback: idk, not sure hwat this impacts
annotations.resolution: Explain derived-table reuse with an experiment-level mean example. Demand remains unconfirmed.

overall_direction: Unclear or unanswered topics have lower current demonstrated interest; they are not rejected automatically.
